$comment: CANONICAL /build-marker.txt SAMPLES — the SHARED corpus for every parser of that file.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (#3730). The two live consoles serve markers in DIFFERENT
shapes, and nothing recorded that. Measured 2026-08-18 by unauthenticated HTTPS
GET against both estates:
Commercial  sha=09ac2517e8139f4fb6dff87ff2dac6c029b7f8d0  stamp=20260818T152007Z
Government  sha=28de89fb                                  stamp=2026-08-11T09:23:46Z
Both the SHA LENGTH and the STAMP FORMAT differ, and the difference is
structural rather than accidental — it comes from the producers:
.github/workflows/build-fiab-images-acr-tasks.yml:447
--build-arg LOOM_BUILD_SHA=${{ github.sha }}          -> 40 hex
.github/workflows/gov-build-images.yml:208,337
SHA_TAG=$(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)               -> 8 hex
Both are written by apps/fiab-console/Dockerfile:152 into /app/public/build-marker.txt.
A parser tested against ONE cloud's shape is a parser that has never been shown
to read the OTHER cloud — which is the cloud-parity.md failure this issue is
about. So both the CI alarm (scripts/ci/__tests__/cross-cloud-drift.test.mjs)
and the console (apps/fiab-console/lib/admin/__tests__/estate-fleet.test.ts)
assert against THIS file. Two implementations, one corpus: they cannot drift
apart on format handling without a test going red.
`unparseable` is the half that matters most. Per deploy-integrity.md R7 an
unreadable marker must produce a NAMED failure, never a default. If a parser
quietly returned no sha for any of these, the caller would compute zero commits
behind and a broken estate would render as a current one — an UNKNOWN reported
as a healthy result, which this repo has shipped three separate times.

real.note: Live https://csa-loom.limitlessdata.ai/build-marker.txt, read 2026-08-18. Full 40-hex github.sha, compact basic-ISO stamp.

Live https://loom-console-dcmt6cqoezlgs-agg6h9e5cjamh5h2.z01.azurefd.us/build-marker.txt, read 2026-08-18. ABBREVIATED 8-hex sha, extended-ISO stamp. This is the row that the Commercial-only parser shape would have had to guess at.
Same bytes without the trailing newline — a parser anchored on \n would read the token into the stamp.
The shortest abbreviation git will produce by default. Accepted; six is not (see unparseable/sha-too-short).
git accepts an uppercase object id; so must the parser, or a legitimate build reads as malformed.

The Dockerfile ARG default for the TIMESTAMP only. The sha is real, so the drift verdict is still computable — a missing stamp must NOT invalidate the marker. `stamp` degrades to null; `sha` survives.

The same marker with CRLF terminators. It MUST parse — a CR that leaked into the value would be carried into `git cat-file` and into a compare URL, and CR-carrying values have broken loops in this repo before (az -o tsv). Pinned as a REAL case, not a failure: the field terminator is whitespace, and \r is whitespace, so the value comes back clean.

unparseable.note: A 200 with an empty body. Naming no commit, it must not resolve to zero-behind.

A WAF / Front Door / ingress error page answering 200 with HTML. This is the realistic way a marker probe gets a body that is not a marker, and reading it as 'no drift' would report a DOWN estate as a current one.

Our services aren't available right now

We're working to restore all services as soon as possible. Please check back soon.

unparseable.note: A marker whose sha= field is absent entirely.

apps/fiab-console/Dockerfile:41 `ARG LOOM_BUILD_SHA=unknown` — what the image carries when CI passed no build-arg at all. It names no commit, so it is unparseable, not a sha. readBuildMarker() in lib/updates/current-version.ts already drops this exact value; every parser must.
`--build-arg LOOM_BUILD_SHA=` expands to an empty field.
Six hex. Below git's 7-character abbreviation floor and far too ambiguous to name a commit.
41 hex — one past a full object id.
A branch name rather than an object id.

The exact SSRF payload documented at app/api/admin/deploy-status/route.ts (GIT_OBJECT_ID). Interpolated into an api.github.com path the WHATWG URL parser collapses the ../ segments BEFORE the request goes out, so the marker chooses the endpoint. It must be rejected as unparseable and its bytes must never reach a URL.
